page_note: This is the famous autobiographical prologue of the Kephalaia: Mani's first-person revelation list (a 'table of contents' of mysteries shown to him) followed by biographical narrative (Artaxerxes' last years, mission to India, Shapur's accession, audience at court). NO cosmological substrate teaching is present. The substrate TOPICS are named (Light/Darkness, ships, molding of Adam, Tree of Knowledge) but not taught — they are catalogued as content of revelation, wrapped entirely in apostolic frame syntax 'He revealed to me / He opened my eyes / He informed me'. Segments 14-17 explicitly invoke institutional categories (apostles selecting churches, Elect, catechumens, commandments). Segments 24-35 are pure hagiographic biography. The high apparent ecclesial density in the first half (segs 14-17) and its absence in the second half corresponds simply to the structural shift from revelation-catalogue to mission-biography, not to substrate→overlay drift.

segments.temporal_note: First-person revelation frame: '...with me. He revealed to me concerning the mystery'. This is Mani's autobiographical voice introducing the catalogue of revealed mysteries.
'Hidden from the worlds and the generations: the mystery of the Deep' — names a substrate topic but does not teach it; pure revelation-list framing.
'He revealed to me the mystery of the Light' — autobiographical revelation formula.
Continues the catalogue: '...and the Darkness — the mystery of the clash of fighting and the war'. Substrate topic named, not taught.
'The war that the Darkness unleashed forth' — still within the revelation catalogue.
'He also revealed to me in what manner the Light...' — explicit revelation formula.
Continuation of revelation-list; describes content but in catalogue voice not teaching voice.
'He also opened my eyes concerning the manner in which the ships were established' — revelation formula about ships, but ships themselves not taught here.
Continuation: gods of Light refine Light through ships — catalogued summary of substrate cosmology, embedded in Mani's revelation autobiography.
'The Erring itself, with the bringing-forth' — substrate topic named in catalogue.
'Mystery of the molding of Adam' — substrate topic named in revelation list.
'He also informed me concerning the mystery of the Tree of Knowledge' — explicit revelation formula.
Brief gloss on Adam eating from Tree, then 'The myste-' begins next entry in catalogue.
'The mystery of the apostles who are sent to the worlds' — apostolic mission category, transitions to ecclesial section.
⚠ SEAM flagged. 'They elect the churches; the mystery of the Elect' — explicit institutional vocabulary (ⲛⲉⲕⲕⲗⲏⲥⲓⲁ, ⲛⲉⲕⲗⲉⲕⲧⲟⲥ). One side reaches into Manichaean church structure.
'Their commandments' — continuation of the ecclesial mystery-list (commandments of the Elect).
'Mystery of the catechumens, of their helpers' — explicit ⲕⲁⲧⲏⲭⲟⲩⲙⲉⲛⲟⲥ; institutional category.
'Their commandments; the mystery of the sinners with their works' — institutional/disciplinary category in the church-list.
'And the punishment laid upon them: this is the manner in which everything that has happened' — closes the ecclesial mystery-list with a summary clause.
'What shall happen was revealed to me through the Paraclete' — explicit Manichaean self-claim of Paraclete revelation; pure apostolic frame.
'Everything the eye sees, the ear hears...' — Mani's claim to comprehensive revealed knowledge; apostolic self-portrait.
'I came to know through it' — first-person epistemic claim, revelation autobiography.
'I beheld the All through him, I became one body' — Mani's mystical-unity claim with the Paraclete; classic apostolic frame material.
'And one spirit' — completes the unity formula. End of revelation-prologue unit.
'In the last years of Artaxerxes' — biographical chronology begins. Pure hagiographic frame.
'I came forth to preach. I crossed over to the region of the Indians' — Mani's mission biography.
'I preached to them the hope of life. I selected at that place' — biographical mission narrative.
'A fine selection' — closes the India mission unit; biographical.
'But in the very year' — chronological transition; biographical.
'Ardashir the king died, Shapur his son became king' — historical chronology, hagiographic frame.
'I crossed over from the region of the Indians to the land of the Persians' — biographical itinerary.
'From the land of Persia also I came to the land of Babylon, of Mesene' — biographical itinerary continues.
'And the region of the Khūzians; I appeared before Shapur the king' — biographical, court audience.
'He received me with great honor; he gave me leave to journey' — court hagiography.
'To preach the word of life. I spent some other years' — mission biography.
Damaged tail: 'in the ...status, many years in...' — biographical continuation.
